<description>
`CheckBlock` returns true right away when `block.fChecked` is set. In the kernel API a `btck_Block` wraps a shared `CBlock`, and `btck_block_copy` only adds a reference, so once a block passed `btck_block_check` or `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block`, later calls on it (or on a copy) skip the checks, whatever consensus params or flags are passed. For example a regtest block that has passed once with regtest params also returns 1 from `btck_block_check` with mainnet params.

bitcoind isn't affected, since it only has one chainstate manager and one set of params. `btck_block_check` and custom signet params are new in 32.0, and the header docs don't mention this.

Following sedited's review, this no longer copies the block on every call. It only documents on `btck_block_check` and `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block` that a block caches its check results and should only be used with one set of consensus parameters.
</description>

<commits>
54b363a291 kernel: document that blocks cache their check results

A btck_Block caches the result of its context-free checks, and copies
made with btck_block_copy share that cache. Once a block passed
btck_block_check or btck_chainstate_manager_process_block, later calls
with other consensus parameters or flags are not checked again.

Document that a block should only be used with a single set of
consensus parameters, instead of paying for a copy on every call.

47cb9a682b kernel: limit cache docs to blocks checked for POW and merkle root

The cache is only set if both the proof of work and the merkle root
were checked.

3add4efcd2 kernel: drop POW/merkle clause from process_block docs

btck_chainstate_manager_process_block always checks the proof of work
and the merkle root, so the clause is only needed for btck_block_check.
</commits>
